correctness.rationale: Every active vertex has precisely two active neighbors, so nonempty support is an induced disjoint union of cycles; below 2g vertices it is a single cycle. A chord on a k-cycle creates two cycles whose lengths sum to k+2, forcing k>=2g-2; two attachments from an external vertex create two cycles with sum k+4, forcing k>=2g-4. Therefore for k<2g-4 the correspondence of equilibria and simple cycles is bijective. The theta graph with path lengths (g-2,g-2,2) realizes an excluded external two-neighbor attachment exactly at k=2g-4 and has no other cycle of that length. Standard-library exhaustive enumerations on 16 graphs verify independent finite instances, including Petersen and Heawood and five theta sharpness graphs. The finite tests do not establish the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The minimum number of positive producers in a nontrivial equilibrium is a natural production-cost extremal invariant of the strict game. The theorem determines it and its multiplicity for every graph of girth >=5 and, more strongly, recovers an entire initial segment of the equilibrium producer-count polynomial from ordinary cycle counts. The exact coefficient boundary k=2g-4 is forced by and sharp for a concrete three-path topology, not an arbitrarily selected finite slice. This yields a structural tractable region inside a best-response setting with generally hard equilibrium questions, without asserting welfare claims.
